newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 16.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Monday.

- Only 21 percent of Catholics follow the teaching of their church when it comes to making "serious moral decisions, compared to 78 percent who follow their own consciences, according to an opinion poll.
- The Irish European Union Presidency is hoping to defuse a serious dispute with the United States over Cuba at a summit meeting in Washington on Monday with President Clinton.
- Economic growth in Dublin exceeded that of any other major European city in 1996, according to a new report from the Dublin Chamber of Commerce.
- Ireland's President, Mary Robinson, and the Irish government argued over who should carry out the duties of welcoming EU leaders at a lunch during the weekend summit, it emerged on Sunday night.

- Ireland's Arts Minister, Michael D.Higgins, wants 10 percent of all TV and radio programmes to be in the Irish language and sporting bodies to give Ireland's national broadcasting company, RTE, first option on major events.

- The number of non Irish-resident tourists to visit Dublin grew by 20 percent in 1996 to 2.5 million, equivalent to two-and-a-half times the population of the city, according to a report on the capital's economy published on Sunday by the Dublin Chamber of Commerce.
